VIM ships the two pieces a fair imputation benchmark needs: `makeMissing()`
generates missingness with a **known mechanism** in complete data, and
`evaluation()`/`nrmse()` score imputations against the withheld truth. This
vignette wires them into a small but complete benchmark harness. The chunks
below were run when the vignette was precomputed (`vignettes/precompute.R` in
the source repository; the code is shown unchanged and runs as is) with


``` r
NREP <- 3     # replications per mechanism -- demo scale!
N    <- 300   # rows drawn from the complete data
```

Three replications only make a smoke test, not evidence: rerun with
`NREP <- 200` (identical code) for stable rankings; that is the setting used
for the accompanying paper.

## Data and scenarios

The `tao` data (Tropical Atmosphere Ocean project) offer strongly correlated
real measurements — exactly the structure conditional imputation can exploit.


``` r
library(VIM)
set.seed(2026)

data(tao, package = "VIM")
vars  <- c("Sea.Surface.Temp", "Air.Temp", "Humidity", "UWind", "VWind")
full  <- na.omit(tao[, vars])
targets <- c("Sea.Surface.Temp", "Air.Temp", "Humidity")
nrow(full)
#> [1] 565
```

Each replication draws `N` rows, amputes 20% of the three target variables
under MCAR or MAR (missingness driven by the observed wind variables), lets
every method impute, and scores the per-variable NRMSE on the amputed cells.

## The harness

Each method is one function `data.frame -> data.frame`; adding a competitor
is one more list entry. The cellwise entry uses the cell-weighted MM
regression engine (`engine = "cellwise-mm"`), which does not require the
optional `crmReg` package. The first scenario has numeric targets; the mixed-data
scenario below also evaluates binary and multiclass targets using
`classif.cellwise`. Regression-only parameters are supplied per numeric target
so they are not passed to the classifier.


``` r
methods <- list(
  "VIM ranger" = function(d) {
    vimpute(d, spec = list(.default = vs_ranger(num.trees = 100)),
            sequential = FALSE, imp_var = FALSE, verbose = FALSE)
  },
  "VIM robust" = function(d) {
    suppressWarnings(
      vimpute(d, method = "robust", sequential = FALSE,
              imp_var = FALSE, verbose = FALSE))
  },
  "VIM cellwise" = function(d) {
    numeric_targets <- names(d)[vapply(d, function(x) is.numeric(x) && anyNA(x),
                                       logical(1))]
    params <- setNames(lapply(numeric_targets, function(v)
      list(engine = "cellwise-mm")), numeric_targets)
    # A failed learner must not silently turn this benchmark into a test
    # of vimpute's fallback method.
    withCallingHandlers(
      vimpute(d, method = "cellwise", learner_params = params,
              sequential = FALSE, imp_var = FALSE, verbose = FALSE),
      warning = function(w) {
        if (grepl("fallback|falling back|not supported|ignored",
                  conditionMessage(w), ignore.case = TRUE)) stop(w)
      })
  },
  "VIM kNN" = function(d) kNN(d, k = 5, imp_var = FALSE)
)
if (has_mice) {
  methods[["mice (default)"]] <- function(d) {
    mice::complete(mice::mice(d, m = 1, maxit = 5, printFlag = FALSE))
  }
}
if (has_missRanger) {
  methods[["missRanger"]] <- function(d) {
    missRanger::missRanger(d, num.trees = 100, verbose = 0)
  }
}

score_run <- function(truth, amputed, imputed) {
  w <- attr(amputed, "where")
  vapply(targets, function(v) {
    nrmse(x = truth[[v]], y = imputed[[v]], m = w[, v])
  }, numeric(1))
}

run_benchmark <- function(mechanism) {
  out <- list()
  for (r in seq_len(NREP)) {
    # Fix the sampled data independently of each method's RNG consumption.
    run_seed <- 2026L + r + if (mechanism == "MAR") 10000L else 0L
    set.seed(run_seed)
    truth <- full[sample(nrow(full), N), ]
    amp <- makeMissing(truth, prop = 0.2, mechanism = mechanism,
                       vars = targets, seed = 1000 + r)
    for (mth in names(methods)) {
      set.seed(run_seed + 100000L)
      t0 <- proc.time()[["elapsed"]]
      imp <- as.data.frame(methods[[mth]](amp))
      secs <- proc.time()[["elapsed"]] - t0
      out[[length(out) + 1L]] <- data.frame(
        mechanism = mechanism, rep = r, method = mth,
        nrmse = mean(score_run(truth, amp, imp)), seconds = secs)
    }
  }
  do.call(rbind, out)
}
```

## Numeric-data results


``` r
res <- rbind(run_benchmark("MCAR"), run_benchmark("MAR"))
```


``` r
summary_tab <- aggregate(cbind(nrmse, seconds) ~ method + mechanism,

summary_tab <- summary_tab[order(summary_tab$mechanism, summary_tab$nrmse), ]
knitr::kable(summary_tab, digits = 3, row.names = FALSE,
```

## Mixed-data scenario

This reproducible synthetic population contains two fully observed numeric
predictors (`x`, `z`), one fully observed categorical predictor (`group`),
and three targets: a continuous response, a binary factor, and a three-level
factor. All targets depend on the predictors, with independent response noise;
no target is simply a discretized copy of another target. The data are clean:
this evaluates mixed-data imputation, not resistance to cellwise contamination.


``` r
set.seed(7301)
npop <- 2000L
mixed_full <- data.frame(x = rnorm(npop), z = rnorm(npop),
                         group = factor(sample(c("a", "b", "c"), npop, TRUE)))
g <- as.numeric(mixed_full$group) - 2
mixed_full$continuous <- 2 + 1.5 * mixed_full$x - mixed_full$z + .5 * g +
  rnorm(npop, sd = .7)
pr_binary <- plogis(1.5 * mixed_full$x - mixed_full$z + .5 * g)
mixed_full$binary <- factor(ifelse(runif(npop) < pr_binary, "yes", "no"),
                            levels = c("no", "yes"))
eta <- cbind(low = -mixed_full$x + .4 * g,
             middle = .5 * mixed_full$z,
             high = mixed_full$x - .5 * mixed_full$z - .4 * g)
prob <- exp(eta - apply(eta, 1, max))
prob <- prob / rowSums(prob)
mixed_full$category <- factor(vapply(seq_len(npop), function(i)
  sample(colnames(prob), 1, prob = prob[i, ]), character(1)),
  levels = colnames(prob))
mixed_targets <- c("continuous", "binary", "category")
```

Each replication samples `N` rows and amputes 20% of each target under MCAR
or MAR. MAR probabilities depend only on the fully observed `x` and `z`.
We report continuous-target NRMSE and the **proportion falsely classified
(PFC)** separately for the binary and multiclass targets. PFC is the fraction
of withheld labels imputed incorrectly; lower is better for every metric.
No categorical label is scored as a numeric code, and PFC is not averaged
with NRMSE. `mice (default)` uses its type-specific defaults: PMM for the
numeric target, logistic regression for the binary target, and multinomial
regression for the unordered three-level target.


``` r
run_mixed_benchmark <- function(mechanism) {
  out <- list()
  for (r in seq_len(NREP)) {
    run_seed <- 7301L + r + if (mechanism == "MAR") 10000L else 0L
    set.seed(run_seed)
    truth <- mixed_full[sample(nrow(mixed_full), N), ]
    amp <- makeMissing(truth, prop = .2, mechanism = mechanism,
      vars = mixed_targets, seed = 3000L + r,
      weights = if (mechanism == "MAR") c(x = 1, z = -.5) else NULL)
    w <- attr(amp, "where")
    stopifnot(all(colSums(w[, mixed_targets, drop = FALSE]) > 0),
              !any(w[, c("x", "z", "group")]))
    for (mth in names(methods)) {
      set.seed(run_seed + 100000L)
      t0 <- proc.time()[["elapsed"]]
      imp <- as.data.frame(methods[[mth]](amp))
      secs <- proc.time()[["elapsed"]] - t0
      stopifnot(nrow(imp) == nrow(truth), !anyNA(imp),
                all(is.finite(imp$continuous)))
      for (v in names(truth)) {
        stopifnot(all(as.character(imp[[v]][!w[, v]]) ==
                        as.character(truth[[v]][!w[, v]])))
      }
      pfc_target <- function(v) {
        stopifnot(is.factor(imp[[v]]),
                  identical(levels(imp[[v]]), levels(truth[[v]])))
        mean(as.character(imp[[v]][w[, v]]) !=
               as.character(truth[[v]][w[, v]]))
      }
      out[[length(out) + 1L]] <- data.frame(
        mechanism = mechanism, rep = r, method = mth,
        nrmse = nrmse(truth$continuous, imp$continuous, m = w[, "continuous"]),
        pfc_binary = pfc_target("binary"),
        pfc_multiclass = pfc_target("category"), seconds = secs)
    }
  }
  do.call(rbind, out)
}
```

## Mixed-data results

All methods retain the same single-pass/iteration and uncertainty settings
used above. In particular, vimpute uses its default uncertainty setting:
categorical imputations are draws from predicted class probabilities, rather
than deterministic most-probable labels. Consequently, these scores compare
the configured imputation procedures, not just classifier discrimination.


``` r
mixed_res <- rbind(run_mixed_benchmark("MCAR"), run_mixed_benchmark("MAR"))
stopifnot(nrow(mixed_res) == 2L * NREP * length(methods),
          all(is.finite(as.matrix(mixed_res[c("nrmse", "pfc_binary",
                                              "pfc_multiclass", "seconds")]))),
          all(mixed_res$pfc_binary >= 0 & mixed_res$pfc_binary <= 1),
          all(mixed_res$pfc_multiclass >= 0 & mixed_res$pfc_multiclass <= 1))
```


``` r
mixed_summary <- aggregate(cbind(nrmse, pfc_binary, pfc_multiclass, seconds) ~
                             method + mechanism, data = mixed_res, FUN = mean)
mixed_summary <- mixed_summary[order(mixed_summary$mechanism,
                                     mixed_summary$pfc_multiclass), ]
knitr::kable(mixed_summary, digits = 3, row.names = FALSE,
  caption = sprintf("Mixed-data mean NRMSE, binary/multiclass PFC, and runtime (seconds), %d replications -- demo scale.", NREP))
```

## Cellwise-contamination scenario

We repeat the mixed-data experiment with **0%, 5%, and 10% contamination**
in the observed numeric cells (`x`, `z`, and `continuous`). For each column,
a randomly selected fraction of its observed cells receives an additive shift
of **eight clean-column standard deviations**, with independently sampled
positive or negative signs. Cells are selected independently across columns,
not by selecting entire rows. Categorical labels are not corrupted.

Missingness is generated from the clean data first. The missingness mask,
clean truth, sampled rows, and imputation seeds are paired across contamination
levels and methods; the 5% contaminated set is nested in the 10% set. The clean
baseline reuses the mixed-data runs above. Shifts are applied only to observed
cells, including observed predictors of rows requiring imputation. Thus this
is a stress test of both robust fitting and prediction with contaminated
predictors, not just robustness to contaminated training responses. The cellwise learners use training-median replacement for grossly outlying
numeric predictor cells at prediction time (`clean_predictors = TRUE`,
`predictor_cutoff = 4.5`). Their training fit retains the original design and
cell weights. Cellwise PMM also screens donors using training-calibrated
response residuals (`donor_cutoff = 4.5`), so robust fitting is not undone by
drawing a grossly contaminated observed response. Set `clean_predictors = FALSE`
and `donor_cutoff = Inf` to recover the earlier prediction/donor behavior.
These safeguards use no clean truth or simulation contamination labels.

All scores use the **original, uncontaminated truth at the originally missing
cells**. Corrupted observed cells are not scored as imputation errors, and
methods must preserve their supplied observed values. Clean scales are used
only to construct the simulation's contamination, never supplied to a learner.


``` r
contamination_rates <- c(.05, .10)
shift_sd <- 8
run_contaminated_benchmark <- function(mechanism) {
  out <- list()
  for (r in seq_len(NREP)) {
    # Match the clean mixed-data scenario exactly.
    run_seed <- 7301L + r + if (mechanism == "MAR") 10000L else 0L
    set.seed(run_seed)
    truth <- mixed_full[sample(nrow(mixed_full), N), ]
    amp <- makeMissing(truth, prop = .2, mechanism = mechanism,
      vars = mixed_targets, seed = 3000L + r,
      weights = if (mechanism == "MAR") c(x = 1, z = -.5) else NULL)
    w <- attr(amp, "where")
    numeric_cols <- c("x", "z", "continuous")
    set.seed(run_seed + 200000L)
    plan <- lapply(numeric_cols, function(v) {
      observed <- which(!w[, v])
      list(rows = sample(observed, length(observed)),
           signs = sample(c(-1, 1), length(observed), replace = TRUE),
           scale = sd(truth[[v]]))
    })
    names(plan) <- numeric_cols
    for (rate in contamination_rates) {
      corrupted <- amp
      contaminated <- matrix(FALSE, nrow(amp), ncol(amp),
                              dimnames = list(NULL, names(amp)))
      for (v in numeric_cols) {
        k <- floor(rate * length(plan[[v]]$rows))
        ids <- plan[[v]]$rows[seq_len(k)]
        corrupted[[v]][ids] <- corrupted[[v]][ids] +
          shift_sd * plan[[v]]$scale * plan[[v]]$signs[seq_len(k)]
        contaminated[ids, v] <- TRUE
        stopifnot(sum(contaminated[, v]) == k)
      }
      stopifnot(!any(contaminated & w), identical(is.na(corrupted), is.na(amp)))
      for (mth in names(methods)) {
        set.seed(run_seed + 100000L)
        t0 <- proc.time()[["elapsed"]]
        imp <- as.data.frame(methods[[mth]](corrupted))
        secs <- proc.time()[["elapsed"]] - t0
        stopifnot(nrow(imp) == nrow(truth), !anyNA(imp),
                  all(is.finite(imp$continuous)))
        for (v in names(truth)) {
          stopifnot(all(as.character(imp[[v]][!w[, v]]) ==
                          as.character(corrupted[[v]][!w[, v]])))
        }
        pfc_target <- function(v) {
          stopifnot(is.factor(imp[[v]]),
                    identical(levels(imp[[v]]), levels(truth[[v]])))
          mean(as.character(imp[[v]][w[, v]]) !=
                 as.character(truth[[v]][w[, v]]))
        }
        out[[length(out) + 1L]] <- data.frame(
          mechanism = mechanism, rep = r, method = mth,
          nrmse = nrmse(truth$continuous, imp$continuous, m = w[, "continuous"]),
          pfc_binary = pfc_target("binary"),
          pfc_multiclass = pfc_target("category"), seconds = secs,
          contamination = rate)
      }
    }
  }
  do.call(rbind, out)
}
```


``` r
contamination_res <- rbind(transform(mixed_res, contamination = 0),
  run_contaminated_benchmark("MCAR"), run_contaminated_benchmark("MAR"))
stopifnot(nrow(contamination_res) == 2L * NREP * length(methods) * 3L,
  all(is.finite(as.matrix(contamination_res[c("nrmse", "pfc_binary",
                                             "pfc_multiclass", "seconds")]))),
  all(contamination_res$pfc_binary >= 0 & contamination_res$pfc_binary <= 1),
  all(contamination_res$pfc_multiclass >= 0 & contamination_res$pfc_multiclass <= 1))
# Pair each run with its own clean baseline before averaging changes.
key <- function(d) paste(d$mechanism, d$rep, d$method, sep = ":")
clean <- contamination_res[contamination_res$contamination == 0, ]
stopifnot(!anyDuplicated(key(clean)))
idx <- match(key(contamination_res), key(clean))
stopifnot(!anyNA(idx))
for (metric in c("nrmse", "pfc_binary", "pfc_multiclass")) {
  contamination_res[[paste0("delta_", metric)]] <-
    contamination_res[[metric]] - clean[[metric]][idx]
}
```


``` r
contamination_summary <- aggregate(
  cbind(nrmse, pfc_binary, pfc_multiclass, seconds) ~ method + mechanism + contamination,
  data = contamination_res, FUN = mean)
contamination_summary <- contamination_summary[order(contamination_summary$mechanism,
  contamination_summary$contamination, contamination_summary$nrmse), ]
knitr::kable(contamination_summary, digits = 3, row.names = FALSE,
  caption = "Mean scores under numeric cellwise contamination (0, 0.05, 0.10); lower is better.")
```

``` r
local({
  old_par <- par(mfrow = c(1, 3))
  on.exit(par(old_par))
  d <- degradation[degradation$mechanism == "MAR" & degradation$contamination == .10, ]
  metrics <- c(delta_nrmse = "Continuous target", delta_pfc_binary = "Binary target",
               delta_pfc_multiclass = "Multiclass target")
  for (metric in names(metrics)) {
    ranked <- d[order(d[[metric]]), ]
    dotchart(rev(ranked[[metric]]), labels = rev(ranked$method), pch = 19,
      main = metrics[[metric]], xlab = "Change vs clean (MAR, 10% contaminated)",
      xlim = range(c(0, ranked[[metric]])))
    abline(v = 0, lty = 2, col = "grey60")
  }
})
```

![plot of chunk contamination-mar-dotchart](figures/benchmark-contamination-mar-dotchart-1.png)

Small degradation alone is not evidence of good imputation: compare the
absolute scores as well as changes from each method's clean baseline.
The methods were not tuned for this contamination model. This demo does not
establish a general robustness ranking, and it does not evaluate corrupted
categorical labels or recovery of the observed contaminated cells.

At this demo scale the rankings are indicative only. More replications and
Monte Carlo uncertainty estimates are needed for substantive comparisons;
`NREP <- 200` is a useful larger run, not a guarantee of negligible uncertainty.
Other packages drop in the same way, for example a `mixgb` entry when installed.

## Notes on fairness

- All methods see identical amputed datasets (`seed` in `makeMissing()`).
  Sampling and method runs have explicit replication seeds, so adding a
  method does not change the data or random draws seen by the others.
- NRMSE is computed on the amputed cells only, against the withheld truth,
  and is scale-free (RMSE divided by the standard deviation of the true
  values), so it can be averaged over variables.
- Point-prediction accuracy is *one* criterion; it systematically favours
  conditional-mean methods over draw-based ones. For inference the relevant
  yardstick is the coverage of pooled confidence intervals -- see the
  companion vignette *Validating multiple-imputation properness*.
- `overimpute()` provides the complementary calibration check on real data
  where no truth is available.
